|date=July 2026 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{cite web |title=Active pharmaceutical ingredients |url=https://ipca.com/active-pharmaceutical-ingredient-products/ |publisher=Ipca Laboratories Ltd. |access-date=3 August 2026}} Ipca is one of the largest global suppliers of the antimalarials [[hydroxychloroquine]] and [[chloroquine]], as well as of APIs such as [[atenolol]], [[chlorthalidone]], [[losartan]] and [[metoprolol]].{{cite news |last=Basu |first=Himani Chandna |title=Govt places order for 10 crore hydroxychloroquine tablets with Ipca labs and Zydus Cadila |url=https://theprint.in/health/govt-places-order-for-10-crore-hydroxychloroquine-tablets-with-ipca-labs-and-zydus-cadila/395248/ |work=[[ThePrint]] |date=4 April 2020 |access-date=3 August 2026}} Since 2023, it has held a majority stake in [[Unichem Laboratories]].{{cite news |title=Ipca Laboratories acquires 19.29% stake in Unichem through open offer |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/ipca-laboratories-acquires-19-29-stake-in-unichem-through-open-offer-123092100942_1.html |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=21 September 2023 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The company is listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange|BSE]] and the [[National Stock Exchange of India]], and reported consolidated revenue of {{INRConvert|9646|c}} in the financial year ended 31 March 2026. ==History== ===Formation and early years=== The company was incorporated in Mumbai on 19 October 1949 as The Indian Pharmaceutical Combine Association Limited by a group of businessmen and medical professionals, and adopted its present name, Ipca Laboratories, in 1964. It commissioned a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Mumbai in 1969 and began marketing formulations in the domestic market in 1976. ===Godha and Bachchan ownership=== In 1975, control of the then loss-making company was acquired by a group that included [[chartered accountant]] Premchand Godha, film actor [[Amitabh Bachchan]], Ajitabh Bachchan, [[Jaya Bachchan]] and M. R. Chandurkar.{{cite web |url=http://www.indiainfoline.com/Markets/Company/Background/Company-Profile/Ipca-Laboratories-Ltd/524494 |title=Ipca Laboratories Ltd Background details about Company Profile |publisher=Indiainfoline.com |date=9 August 1988 |access-date=1 December 2010}}{{cite news |title=Meet Amitabh Bachchan's former CA, who built a ₹28,000 crore pharma giant |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/trends/story/meet-amitabh-bachchans-former-ca-who-built-a-rs28000-crore-pharma-giant-543814-2026-07-19 |work=[[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] |date=19 July 2026 |access-date=3 August 2026}} Godha, who had handled the Bachchan family's finances, joined the board in October 1975 and became managing director in 1983, when the company's turnover was about ₹54 lakh. Ipca commissioned its first API plant at [[Ratlam]], Madhya Pradesh, in 1984 and became a public limited company in 1993. In 1997, the Bachchan family agreed to sell its 36% holding in Ipca to the company's four whole-time directors, and had exited the company by 1999.{{Cite news |last=Tiwari |first=Vibha |date=7 February 1997 |title=Bachchans To Sell 36% Stake In Ipca Labs To Directors |work=Business Standard India |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/specials/bachchans-to-sell-36-stake-in-ipca-labs-to-directors-197020701081_1.html |access-date=16 July 2022}} The Godha family has led the company since; {{as of|2026|lc=y}}, Premchand Godha serves as executive chairman, with his sons Pranay Godha and Prashant Godha on the board alongside managing director and CFO Ajit Kumar Jain. In 2004, [[Forbes]] selected Ipca for the second consecutive year as one of the 200 'Best under a billion' companies in Asia. ===Expansion and acquisitions=== Ipca acquired Onyx Scientific, a [[contract development and manufacturing organisation]] based in [[Sunderland]], United Kingdom, in 2011.{{cite news |title=Ipca Acquires Onyx Scientific |url=https://www.contractpharma.com/contents/view_breaking-news/2011-08-09/ipca-acquires-onyx-scientific |work=Contract Pharma |date=9 August 2011 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In 2013, it agreed to buy a 50% stake in Avik Pharmaceutical, a Vapi-based maker of steroid and hormone APIs.{{cite news |title=IPCA Lab gains on plans to acquire 50% stake in a pharma firm |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/ipca-lab-gains-on-plans-to-acquire-50-stake-in-a-pharma-firm-113111900130_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=19 November 2013 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In 2015, it launched an open offer to raise its holding in Krebs Biochemicals & Industries, an Andhra Pradesh-based API manufacturer that became an associate company.{{cite news |title=Ipca Labs starts open offer for Krebs Biochemicals |url=https://www.business-standard.com/content/b2b-pharma/ipca-labs-starts-open-offer-for-krebs-biochemicals-115041500148_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=15 April 2015 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In January 2018, Ipca acquired Pisgah Laboratories, a North Carolina-based API contract manufacturer, for US$9.65 million through its US and UK subsidiaries.{{cite news |title=Ipca Laboratories acquires US-based API developer Pisgah Labs for $9.65 mn |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ipca-laboratories-acquires-us-based-api-developer-pisgah-labs-for-9-65-mn-118011700281_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=17 January 2018 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The company has also built up a stake in the listed drugmaker [[Lyka Labs]], which reached 40.98% in April 2024 following the conversion of warrants.{{cite news |title=Ipca Laboratories hikes stake in Lyka Labs |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/ipca-laboratories-hikes-stake-in-lyka-labs-124041700645_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=17 April 2024 |access-date=3 August 2026}} Ipca's largest acquisition came in 2023, when it agreed to buy a 33.38% promoter stake in [[Unichem Laboratories]], completing the purchase in August 2023 for {{INRConvert|945|c}}, and acquired a further 19.29% through a mandatory open offer for {{INRConvert|597.5|c}}, taking its holding to 52.67%.{{cite news |title=Ipca to acquire 33.4% stake in Unichem Labs for Rs 1,034 cr at Rs 440 per share |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/ipca-to-acquire-334-stake-in-unichem-labs-for-rs-1034-cr-at-rs-440-per-share-378647-2023-04-24 |work=Business Today |date=24 April 2023 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The [[Competition Commission of India]] approved the acquisition subject to voluntary modifications offered by the company.{{cite web |title=CCI Approves Acquisition of 59.38% Shareholding in Unichem Laboratories by Ipca Laboratories Subject to Certain Voluntary Modifications |url=https://www.azbpartners.com/bank/cci-approves-acquisition-of-59-38-shareholding-in-unichem-laboratories-by-ipca-laboratories-subject-to-certain-voluntary-modifications/ |publisher=AZB & Partners |date=2023 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The transaction made Unichem's subsidiaries in the United States, United Kingdom, Ireland, South Africa, Brazil and China part of the Ipca group. In 2024, the group consolidated its United States generics business by transferring the operations of Bayshore Pharmaceuticals, Ipca's wholly owned US subsidiary, to Unichem Pharmaceuticals (USA).{{cite news |title=Unichem Labs shares jump 4% after announcing consolidation of US generics |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/unichem-labs-shares-jump-4-after-announcing-consolidation-of-us-generics-124092300251_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=23 September 2024 |access-date=3 August 2026}} ===United States regulatory issues=== Following a 2014 inspection of its Ratlam API plant, the US [[Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) raised concerns about [[data integrity]] in the company's laboratory records, and Ipca voluntarily suspended API shipments to the United States.{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Eric |title=FDA warning to Ipca Labs shines light on rampant data falsification |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/fda-warning-to-ipca-labs-shines-light-on-rampant-data-falsification |work=[[Fierce Pharma]] |date=February 2016 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The FDA placed the Ratlam plant under an import alert in January 2015, and extended import alerts to the company's formulation plants at Pithampur (SEZ Indore) and Piparia ([[Silvassa]]) in March 2015.{{cite news |title=Ipca Labs stock slumps 9% on FDA import alert for Ratlam plant |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/ipca-labs-stock-slumps-9-on-fda-import-alert-for-ratlam-plant-115012300493_1.html |agency=[[Press Trust of India]] |work=Business Standard |date=23 January 2015 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{cite news |title=US FDA issues import alert to 2 plants of IPCA Laboratories |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/us-fda-issues-import-alert-to-2-plants-of-ipca-laboratories-115032500427_1.html |agency=Press Trust of India |work=Business Standard |date=25 March 2015 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In January 2016, the agency issued a warning letter covering all three plants, citing systematic manipulation and deletion of failed test results. During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] in March 2020, the FDA temporarily exempted Ipca's hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine products from the import alert to secure supplies of the drugs, which were then under investigation as potential COVID-19 treatments; the exemptions were withdrawn later that year.{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Eric |title=FDA frees India's Ipca from import ban so it can ship unproven COVID-19 treatments |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/fda-lifts-ban-so-india-s-ipca-so-can-ship-unproven-covid-19-treatments |work=Fierce Pharma |date=March 2020 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{cite news |title=IPCA Labs says USFDA removes import alert exemption on hydroxychloroquine sulphate |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/ipca-labs-says-usfda-removes-import-alert-exemption-on-hydroxychloroquine-sulphate-120070200594_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=2 July 2020 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In April 2020, the Government of India placed orders for about 100 million hydroxychloroquine tablets with Ipca and [[Zydus Lifesciences|Zydus Cadila]], among the country's largest manufacturers of the drug. The import alerts were lifted in 2023 after fresh FDA inspections; the Ratlam plant's June 2023 inspection was classified "voluntary action indicated" in October 2023.{{cite news |title=Ipca Labs surges 7%, hits 52-week high on favourable report from USFDA |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/ipca-labs-surges-7-hits-52-week-high-on-favourable-report-from-usfda-123102300133_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=23 October 2023 |access-date=3 August 2026}}{{cite web |title=Transcript of earnings conference call held on 10th November 2023 |url=https://www.ipca.com/wp-content/pdf/financials/conferencecall-and-transcripts/transcript-10th-november-2023.pdf |publisher=Ipca Laboratories Ltd. |date=13 November 2023 |access-date=3 August 2026}} After an absence of roughly nine years, the company resumed selling its formulations in the United States, which are distributed through its step-down subsidiary Unichem Pharmaceuticals (USA). ==Operations== ===Formulations=== Ipca manufactures over 350 formulations across dosage forms including tablets, capsules, oral liquids, dry powders and injectables. In India, the company sells branded generics through a field force of more than 6,000 sales and marketing staff, reaching some 200,000 physicians, and its therapeutic strengths include pain management, rheumatology, antimalarials and cardiovascular treatments. Pain management has historically contributed over half of the company's domestic revenue, led by the [[aceclofenac]] brand Zerodol, which had annual sales of around {{INRConvert|500|c}} by 2020.{{cite news |last=Malviya |first=Sagar |title=The Pain Controller |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/specials/indias-best-ceos-2018/story/the-pain-controller-282472-2020-12-24 |work=Business Today |date=24 December 2020 |access-date=3 August 2026}} Several of the company's brands rank among the 300 largest pharmaceutical brands in India.{{cite web |title=About us |url=https://ipca.com/active-pharmaceutical-ingredients-manufacturers-about-us/ |publisher=Ipca Laboratories Ltd. |access-date=3 August 2026}} ===Active pharmaceutical ingredients=== The company produces around 80 APIs, which account for roughly a quarter of its turnover and are exported to more than 70 countries. Ipca describes itself as one of the world's largest suppliers of several APIs, including the antihypertensives atenolol, losartan, metoprolol and [[propranolol]], the diuretics chlorthalidone and [[furosemide]], chloroquine phosphate and hydroxychloroquine sulphate. The API business is backward-integrated with the company's formulations manufacturing. ===Biologics and biosimilars=== Ipca entered the [[biosimilar]] field in 2014 through an alliance with the US biotechnology firm Oncobiologics (later [[Outlook Therapeutics]]) to develop and commercialise [[monoclonal antibody]] biosimilars for oncology and immunology, initially for the Indian and regional markets.{{cite web |title=Oncobiologics and IPCA create biosimilars alliance |url=https://www.gabionline.net/biosimilars/news/Oncobiologics-and-IPCA-create-biosimilars-alliance |publisher=GaBI Online |date=June 2014 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The company subsequently developed biologics manufacturing at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh, supported by biosimilar research and development in Mumbai.{{cite news |title=Ipca Labs Partners BRL to Develop Next-Generation Subcutaneous Biologics for Cancer, Autoimmune Diseases |url=https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/ipca-labs-partners-brl-to-develop-next-generation-subcutaneous-biologics-for-cancer-autoimmune-diseases-172749 |work=Medical Dialogues |date=15 June 2026 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In September 2025, Ipca signed a technology-transfer agreement with the US-based BioSimilar Sciences to develop and commercially manufacture next-generation cancer and anti-inflammatory monoclonal antibody biosimilars at a facility in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico.{{cite news |title=Ipca Laboratories and BioSimilar Sciences sign Technology Transfer Agreement for next-gen cancer and anti-inflammatory biosimilar |url=https://www.businessupturn.com/business/corporates/ipca-laboratories-and-biosimilar-sciences-sign-technology-transfer-agreement-for-next-gen-cancer-and-anti-inflammatory-biosimilar/ |work=Business Upturn |date=24 September 2025 |access-date=3 August 2026}} In June 2026, it signed a global licensing agreement with Bhami's Research Laboratory for a high-concentration [[subcutaneous]] biologics delivery platform for use with monoclonal antibodies in oncology and inflammatory diseases. ===Manufacturing and research=== Ipca operates 16 manufacturing units in India, located across Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Dadra and Nagar Haveli, along with overseas manufacturing at Onyx Scientific in the United Kingdom and Pisgah Laboratories in the United States. During 2025–26, the company closed older facilities at Tarapur, Maharashtra, and Ankleshwar, Gujarat, as part of a consolidation of its manufacturing footprint. Its research and development centres are located at Mumbai, Ratlam, Athal (Silvassa) and Ranu (Vadodara). The company's facilities and products hold approvals from regulators and agencies including the UK [[Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency]], the [[European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines]] and the [[World Health Organization]]. ===Subsidiaries and associates=== Besides Unichem Laboratories, the group's subsidiaries include Onyx Scientific (UK), Pisgah Laboratories (US), Bayshore Pharmaceuticals (US), Trophic Wellness, and marketing and distribution companies in the United States, United Kingdom, Nigeria, Australia, New Zealand and Mexico.{{cite web |title=Ipca Subsidiaries, Joint Venture, and Associates details |url=https://www.indiaratings.co.in/data/Uploads/Others/Subs/Ipca_Subsidiaries.pdf |publisher=[[India Ratings & Research]] |access-date=3 August 2026}} Avik Pharmaceutical is a 50:50 joint venture, while associates include Lyka Labs and Krebs Biochemicals & Industries. ==Finances== For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Ipca reported consolidated revenue from operations of {{INRConvert|9646|c}} and a net profit attributable to shareholders of {{INRConvert|1141|c}}, with slightly more than half of revenue earned outside India.{{cite news |title=Ipca Laboratories Reports 341% Profit Growth In Q4 FY26, Revenue Up 6% |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/ipca-laboratories-reports-341-profit-growth-in-q4-fy26-revenue-up-6 |work=[[The Free Press Journal]] |date=May 2026 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The company had 18,667 permanent employees as of 31 March 2026, and a market capitalisation of approximately {{INRConvert|28000|c}} as of July 2026. ==Sustainability initiatives== Between 2019 and 2023, Ipca invested about {{INRConvert|170|c}} in captive renewable energy projects totalling 36.57 MW – largely solar, along with a 2 MW wind project – across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Silvassa, which replace roughly 26% of the company's power consumption.{{cite web |title=ESG – Renewable Energy |url=https://www.ipca.com/esg-renewable-energy/ |publisher=Ipca Laboratories Ltd. |access-date=3 August 2026}} The company has also begun replacing coal-fired boilers with biomass briquette and pellet fuel, including cultivation of [[napier grass]] as feedstock at [[Wardha]], Maharashtra. In February 2025, Ipca announced a 700-acre manufacturing campus at Wardha, described as Maharashtra's first fully "green" pharmaceutical plant, powered by a 15 MW solar plant and agricultural-waste pellet boilers with no coal usage; its first unit is intended to manufacture chloroquine formulations.{{cite news |title=IPCA Labs to Launch Maharashtra's First Fully Green Pharma Plant in Wardha |url=https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/ipca-labs-to-launch-maharashtras-first-fully-green-pharma-plant-in-wardha-143037 |work=Medical Dialogues |date=10 February 2025 |access-date=3 August 2026}} The company publishes an annual Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report under [[Securities and Exchange Board of India|SEBI]] requirements. In 2024–25, it spent {{INRConvert|20.03|c}} on [[Corporate social responsibility|corporate social responsibility]] programmes, implemented partly through the Ipca Foundation, in areas including education and skill development, healthcare, heritage conservation and environmental protection.{{cite news |title=Ipca Laboratories Spends Rs 20.03 Crore on CSR Initiatives in FY25 |url=https://indiacsr.in/ipca-laboratories-spends-rs-20-03-crore-csr-initiatives-fy25/ |work=India CSR |date=2025 |access-date=3 August 2026}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Nifty 200 companies}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Manufacturing companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Pharmaceutical companies of India]] [[Category:Pharmaceutical companies established in 1949]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1949]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]

Ipca Laboratories Limited is an Indian multinational pharmaceutical company headquartered in Mumbai. The company manufactures and markets more than 350 finished-dosage formulations and around 80 active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), covering therapeutic areas that include pain management, rheumatology, antimalarials, cardiovascular medicine, dermatology and anti-diabetics, and has an emerging biosimilars business. Its products are sold in over 100 countries, and it is one of India's larger API exporters, supplying more than 70 countries.
Ipca is one of the largest global suppliers of the antimalarials hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine, as well as of APIs such as atenolol, chlorthalidone, losartan and metoprolol. Since 2023, it has held a majority stake in Unichem Laboratories. The company is listed on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange of India, and reported consolidated revenue of ₹9,646 crore (US$1.0 billion) in the financial year ended 31 March 2026.
